text:
maya: Quick note from v5-small PTQ: overall NDCG@10 ~flat, but MRR@1/MRR@5 on our short-query cohort dropped ~4%. No tokenization diffs.

anya: ok — same symptom we saw earlier. Does the eval pipeline apply any nondeterministic sort or use unstable argsort?

maya: It uses np.argsort(scores)[::-1] then constructs ranks. Also the candidate loader had shuffle left on from a debug commit.

dmitri: PTQ will collapse tiny differences into quant bins -> more ties/near-ties. MRR (especially top-1) will move even if NDCG@10 is stable.

li: Two directions: (1) deterministic tie-breaker (candidate id / original position), (2) post-quant score calibration (tiny linear scaling or keep last logits at higher precision).

maya: I ran three quick experiments (seeded):
A) no-shuffle + deterministic tiebreak -> MRR gap ~1.0%
B) last-layer fp16 -> MRR gap ~0.5%
C) control (shuffle + no tiebreak) -> MRR gap ~4.1%
NDCG@10 within noise across runs.

anya: can you share a compact histogram summary (FP32 vs PTQ delta) for top-3? even counts of exact-equal would help.

maya: Paste: exact-equal top-3: FP32 0.07%, PTQ 2.0%. deltas <1e-4: FP32 0.8%, PTQ 6.2%. Median abs delta compressed for PTQ.

dmitri: confirms tie clustering. My recommendation: add stable tiebreaker to eval and prod ranking pipeline, add an offline metric "topk_tie_fraction", and add a rankbench smoke that asserts PTQ MRR drop <= 1% on the short-query slice.

li: also propose a "score-resolve" config knob: by default we keep final logits quantized, but allow a fallback to keep last-layer in fp16 for quant schemes that lose too much resolution.

maya: I'll implement tiebreaker + metric and run a final smoke. If results look good I'll open PR with artifacts and a follow-up ticket for the fallback knob.

qa-bot: job-2021: started reproducibility-run (seeded) for maya 10mETA. logs: https://ci.redwood/job/2021

ops-bot: issue created INF-902: "PTQ: short-query MRR regression due to score compression; add tie-breaker, metrics, and last-layer fallback" assigned to maya.

anya: thanks — sounds like a safe path forward instead of reverting PTQ.
